summary: Implemented optional, default-disabled scoring with classifier-only setup, explicit model validation, optional completion routing, and configured classifier invocation and report identity. npm run check passed: 45 test files, 330 tests.

acceptanceCriteria.probe: npm run check: extensions/maestro.integration.test.ts exercises initial setup with available openrouter/typesafe/jev-1.14 and chat model openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol. It verifies selectModel receives only the classifier choice, the scorer model is displayed without thinking, and only setup menus are shown (no thinking prompt). Inspected src/ui/selectClassifier.ts to confirm reuse of the existing picker.

npm run check: extensions/maestro.integration.test.ts verifies confirming the selected classifier saves scorer exactly as {required:true,model:'openrouter/typesafe/jev-1.14'}. Existing first-use parameterized scenarios, including no roles, verify an unselected scorer saves exactly {required:false}. Neither saved form contains thinking.

npm run check: added integration scenarios in src/tools/main/run-builder.integration.test.ts (omitted scorer, verifier and simplifier disabled), run-verifier.integration.test.ts (disabled scorer and simplifier), and run-simplifier.integration.test.ts (disabled scorer after simplifier completion and after completed verification followed by Git-unavailable skipping). All four verify saved candidate-ready, no classifier call, and returned instructions to report scoring as skipped in the final summary. Inspected agents/maestro.md final-summary guidance and src/workflow/transitions.ts optional routing.

npm run check: src/tools/main/score-workflow.integration.test.ts success cases explicitly configure openrouter/typesafe/jev-1.14, verify classifier lookup and invocation, and assert saved provider openrouter and model typesafe/jev-1.14. An additional alternate-provider/custom/judge scenario confirms lookup, invocation, and saved identity follow configuration rather than the former fixed model. Inspected diffs of src/score/requestEvaluation.ts and src/score/scoreWorkflow.ts: existing evaluation logic is reused; questions, evidence collection, normalization, and failure handling are unchanged.

npm run check: extensions/maestro.integration.test.ts parameterized activation scenarios use enabled builder with available model and scorer {required:true} or {required:true,model:''}. Both keep Maestro inactive and assert the activation error identifies the required scorer model.

notes: Required npm run check completed successfully; git diff --check also passed.
